In this Python 3.14 snapshot, the default start method on POSIX platforms other than macOS is `forkserver`. In `library/multiprocessing.rst`, "Contexts and start methods" says that *forkserver* became the default on POSIX platforms in 3.14. It also says the default was changed from *fork* to *forkserver*, and that *fork* is no longer the default on any platform. macOS and Windows default to *spawn*.

An earlier conversation of mine had answered `fork`, which was the pre-3.14 default. That answer does not match this snapshot, so I rechecked the documentation instead of reusing it.

- `library/multiprocessing.rst`
- `library/concurrent.futures.rst` (it also notes the default start method changed away from *fork* in 3.14)
